item.text:
Best read: **mostly no**. The strongest positive evidence is a decline in ordinary criminal cases and one narrow Tibet killing statistic, but the broader 2024 record shows continued political repression, transnational repression, and coercive control in Hong Kong and Xinjiang rather than a clear net safety improvement.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | China sees 25.7-pct drop in criminal cases in 2024 | Ministry of Public Security / Xinhua | 2025-01-11 | https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202501/11/content_WS6781af58c6d0868f4e8eeb6c.html | Official 2024 crime data say criminal cases fell 25.7% and public safety stayed stable. This is the clearest pro-safety item, but it speaks to ordinary crime more than political or intergroup violence. | 3B.10, 3B.6 |
| Positive | 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China (Tibet section) | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128584.html | The report says there were no known reports or credible allegations of arbitrary or unlawful killings in Tibet in 2024. This is a narrow positive on lethal violence, not evidence of broader freedom from repression. | 3B.10, 3B.7 |
| Positive, weak | Counterterrorism Measures Protect Human Rights, Beijing Says | State Council Information Office / China Xinjiang | 2024-01-23 | https://en.chinaxinjiang.cn/2024/01/23/c03755707ff440c3be77630f280ae0a0.html | Beijing claimed its counterterrorism measures were grounded in law and protected human rights. This is self-justifying official framing, not independent proof that insecurity actually fell. | 3B.10, 3B.7, 3B.8 |
| Negative | 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128572.html | The report says China had credible reports of killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, and transnational repression, including mass extrajudicial internment of Uyghurs. It says the government took no credible steps to punish abusers. | 3B.10, 3B.7, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China (Hong Kong) | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128576.html | The Hong Kong chapter says the human rights situation deteriorated, with arbitrary arrest and detention, censorship, transnational repression, and coercive actions against independent trade unions and labor activists. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | US-funded Radio Free Asia shuts Hong Kong bureau, citing security law concerns | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157 | Reuters reported the bureau closed over staff-safety concerns after Article 23, with Hong Kong authorities referring to RFA as a “foreign force.” That is a concrete chilling-effect example. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| Negative | Hong Kong 47 democrats case / mass convictions and pretrial detention | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Reuters reported extensive pretrial detention, denial of bail, and mass convictions in the 47 democrats case. This is direct evidence of selective punishment and political fear rather than protective restraint. | 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.9 |

**Synthesis**
- The pro side is thin and mostly about ordinary criminality, not political or intergroup violence.
- The negative side is stronger and more specific: Hong Kong repression, Xinjiang mass detention/assimilation, and transnational repression show a broader coercive climate.
- I found no credible evidence that Xi’s 2024 governance left citizens broadly safer from political violence, intergroup violence, or preventable domestic insecurity than they were before 2024.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a reliable source showing a broad year-over-year improvement in political violence, intergroup violence, displacement, or fear climate.
- The closest positives are ordinary-crime reduction and a narrow Tibet killing statistic; neither is enough to establish a net safety gain on this lens.
